findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the intent-journal directory to a single unambiguous resolution (e.g. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, matching the existing _quarantine_untracked placement) so the fold-writer and the recovery preamble always agree on where the sentinel lives.
evidence: Plan: journal written 'OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir, so the sentinel itself can never be tree dirt)'
sync.py:253 _quarantine_untracked explicitly uses `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` for exactly the 'outside any working tree' placement, showing the distinction is load-bearing in this codebase
ABSENCE: the plan does not pin common-dir vs per-worktree git-dir for the journal path
findings.finding: The intent-journal location is specified only as 'OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir)', which is ambiguous between the per-worktree git-dir and the common git-dir. The sibling untracked-quarantine code deliberately resolves `--git-common-dir` (sync.py:253); if the fold-writer and the crash-recovery preamble resolve the git dir differently in a linked-worktree tracker, the preamble can miss a live journal and skip the revert it exists to perform.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Crash-atomic compaction fold', intent-journal description
scenarios: A linked-worktree tracker where the compactor writes the journal under one git-dir resolution and the recovery preamble looks under another — the abandoned partial fold is never reverted
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the journal path relative to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (as sync.py:253 already does for the reconverge quarantine), so both writer and recovery preamble resolve the identical location under any worktree layout.

findings.checklist_item: State the dual-write ordering constraint for the marker-untracking migration: land the reconverge + push-recovery variant-(b) recovery before (or atomically with) the untrack commit, or otherwise specify how peers whose HEAD still tracks the markers converge the untrack commit without a variant-(b) abort during active concurrent writes.
evidence: Plan: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers ... via an idempotent ensure unit ... first because every later recovery then only faces untracked artifacts'
RCA (6ccc / e72e): store under 'parallel multi-session writes', ~90 worktrees sharing one .git/HEAD; abort variant (b) is 'tracked .archived deletions'
ABSENCE: plan states ordering ('first') but never states how the untrack COMMIT itself converges with concurrent peers whose HEAD still tracks the markers before variant-(b) recovery lands
findings.finding: The marker-untracking migration ('git rm --cached */.archived */.write.lock' committed to the tickets branch) is sequenced 'first' but the plan does not handle the dual-write window: the store is under active parallel multi-session writes across ~90 worktrees on one shared origin, and the untrack commit is ITSELF a tracked-file deletion (abort variant b) that peers' 'git merge origin/tickets' must absorb. If the ensure unit lands before the reconverge/push-recovery variant-(b) recovery children, the untrack commit can wedge exactly the peers it is meant to heal.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers' (first child); Acceptance Criteria line 3 (git ls-files ... returns empty)
scenarios: Ensure unit commits 'git rm --cached */.archived' and pushes; a peer worktree with those .archived still tracked in HEAD reconverges and its 'git merge origin/tickets' aborts on the tracked-deletion (variant b) before the variant-(b) recovery child has landed
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit sequencing/gating note that the ensure unit's untrack commit is only pushed after the variant-(b) tracked-deletion recovery lands in _union_merge and push_recovery, and add an acceptance-criterion proxy exercising a concurrent peer reconverging against the untrack commit and completing the union merge with no orphaned local commit.

findings.checklist_item: Add a post-migration state assertion (steady state is 'markers untracked on every worktree after next reconverge') and a compensating-forward / back-out note for the untrack commit, rather than asserting only the forward 'git ls-files empty' proxy.
evidence: AC proxy asserts only 'git ls-files '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock' ... returns empty after the ensure unit runs, and marker add/remove churn no longer appears in git status'

ABSENCE: no assertion on post-migration state across peer worktrees and no back-out/compensating-forward path stated; markers are regenerable and 'git rm --cached' preserves working-tree copies so this is not a DATA LOSS RISK, but the reversibility/steady-state across the shared fleet is unstated
findings.finding: The marker-untracking migration is a one-way transformation of the tracked store with no stated back-out path or post-migration state assertion for the fleet of peer worktrees. The AC asserts only the forward state ('git ls-files ... returns empty'); it does not assert what the ~89 peer worktrees' state is after they reconverge with the untrack commit, nor a compensating-forward/back-out plan if the untrack commit needs reverting mid-rollout.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 3; Child 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers'
scenarios: Untrack commit is pushed, some worktrees converge and stop tracking markers while others (paused/offline) still track them, leaving a mixed tracked/untracked steady state that must be asserted or reconciled

evidence: c925 approach: 'window 2 ... the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) is then invoked and takes the write lock itself, converging the previously wedged store'.
c925 AC: 'rebar doctor --repair heals a seeded wedge end-to-end ... merge converged'.

c925's seeded wedge includes 'tracked deletions of store artifacts restorable from HEAD' (class 1) — restored by git checkout before reconverge — but the diverged-origin merge in the end-to-end test can still hit variant (b) which a560 handles.
findings.finding: Dependency gap: child c925-7669-ded8-43a3's doctor --repair end-to-end heal converges the wedged store by invoking sync.reconverge (window 2), which must recover BOTH abort variants — including variant (b) tracked-deletions. That variant-(b) recovery is delivered by sibling a560-85a8-1247-44cd, not by c925 itself, yet the roster encodes no dependency edge from c925 to a560. If c925 lands before a560, its seeded-wedge convergence test can fail on the tracked-deletion abort a560 is meant to fix.
scenarios: c925 merges first; its end-to-end test seeds a diverged origin and a dirty tree, doctor restores class-1 paths then calls reconverge, whose union merge aborts on a variant-(b) local-changes signature that only a560 teaches it to recover — the 'merge converged' AC fails until a560 lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit dependency c925 -> a560 in the deps, and note in c925's approach that its window-1 class-1 restore must clear tracked deletions ahead of reconverge so the merge cannot hit the variant-(b) abort a560 owns.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the intent-journal crash-recovery design (sentinel location, the three-way live/committed/SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT discrimination contract) in an ADR or AGENTS.md / design-doc update so the invariant survives future maintenance.
evidence: "Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL (a commit-pending sentinel): before its first worktree mutation the fold writes an intent record ... OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir)"
The recovery contract encodes a load-bearing invariant ('the retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state has NO journal by construction') with no cited doc/ADR capturing it.
T5e documentation sub-check: a novel architectural decision should be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel architectural pattern — an INTENT JOURNAL (commit-pending sentinel stored outside the worktree under the tracker's git dir) that governs crash-recovery discrimination between half-fold states — but does not state that this design decision will be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update. The three-way recovery contract (live journal + uncommitted snapshot → revert; journal + committed snapshot → discard; SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT has no journal by construction) is subtle enough that future maintainers need a durable record of the invariant.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Crash-atomic compaction fold ... Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL'
scenarios: A future maintainer alters the SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT retention path without knowing the preamble relies on 'no journal by construction', reintroducing the wedge that fsck --repair-snapshots was meant to own.
